hypotheses.justification: This instance is a theorem argument only because it is instance-implicit and its type mentions `R`, which is already an argument. No `omit` removes it, and the statement does not use it. The statement only needs a ring structure on `R`: `X - C c : R[X]` and `.coeff`. The proof works the same without it. `fin_cases i` reduces to `i = 0`, and `coeff (X - C c) 0 = coeff X 0 - coeff (C c) 0 = 0 - c = -c` holds in any (commutative) ring. `simp [coeff_X]` uses `coeff_sub`, `coeff_C` and `coeff_X`, and none of these lemmas needs an algebra structure. No degenerate case causes trouble: if `R` is the zero ring, both sides are 0. So `omit [Algebra ℚ R] in` leaves the theorem true with the same proof.
